recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Compare all-in airfare, one-way/drop fee, connection quality, airport timing, and reimbursement justification before committing.
recovered_habits.default_action: Price SLC-to-first-city and last-city-to-SLC air with a one-way rental, then document the route logic for approval.

evidence.quote: Hi, I’m Tessa. I’m trying to sketch a September recruitment loop from Salt Lake City through Boise, the Palouse, and Spokane. I need to avoid backtracking if we can.
Open-jaw is allowed if there’s a good reason.
If Eugene return is nicer but expensive, how much cheaper would Portland have to be for you to consider driving back?
The Portland round trip may be about $150 cheaper in airfare. Is the backtracking still that bad?
I need to compare open-jaw flying, Dallas round-trip flying, and just driving from Salt Lake with materials.
If my director vetoes the one-way rental drop fee, what is the fallback?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use a round trip or full drive if the open-jaw fare or drop fee is extreme, the return connection is unreliable, or materials make flying impractical.
recovered_habits.name: Use directional open-jaw routing for multi-city work loops when the cost is defensible
recovered_habits.preference_value: Prefers open-jaw flights and one-way rentals over a simple round trip when the event path is directional and a round trip would create backtracking.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work recruitment/admissions loops that start in one metro area and end in another, especially with several cities and a final event far from the arrival airport.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A single connection is acceptable when it is comfortably timed, commonly around an hour or better and preferably 70–90 minutes for work returns.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose nonstop when reasonable; otherwise use one comfortable connection and preserve event/airport buffers even if it costs modestly more.

evidence.quote: Delta is nice if it’s comparable, but schedule matters more. Coach is fine. I’d rather not do more than one connection, and I don’t want a tiny 35-minute layover.
Reliability matters more here. I’m fine getting home around dinner, but I don’t want a long layover or a connection that turns a short return into a whole evening.
I don’t want to gamble the school visit just to save a little.
I do not want to sweat a 35-minute connection out of COS.
I would rather avoid a connection under an hour.
Late is better than sprinting or missing it.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use a cheaper carrier or connection only when the timing, total travel time, and buffer remain comparable; do not choose a tight connection just to save money or fly Delta.
recovered_habits.name: Prioritize flight reliability and comfortable connections over the cheapest fare or preferred carrier
recovered_habits.preference_value: Schedule reliability, sane arrival/departure times, and non-sprinting connections matter more than small fare savings or carrier preference.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Any flight selection, especially work trips with fixed school visits, fairs, receptions, or return deadlines.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Avoid paying extra for preferred windows unless the fee is negligible or reimbursable; avoid Basic when seat selection may become a problem.
recovered_habits.default_action: Select economy/Main Cabin, choose standard no-fee window seats if available, and recheck the seat map at check-in.

evidence.quote: Good. Main cabin/economy, and I’ll pick a window if there’s one. Anything else to note for reimbursement?
Good. Book economy. If seat selection is open, take window on both legs. What should I put in the receipt packet?
Seats are open: 19A outbound and 21F return. Main cabin, not basic.
Good. Can I request window seats without paying extra?
Good point. I also don’t want basic economy if seat selection gets weird.
Pairs first. One window is nice, but I do not want kids separated from an adult.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: When traveling with family, keeping kids with an adult or keeping the group in adjacent pairs overrides the window-seat preference.
recovered_habits.name: Book economy/Main Cabin with standard window seats when practical
recovered_habits.preference_value: Uses economy or Main Cabin, prefers window seats when selectable, and avoids Basic Economy when seat selection or schedule flexibility matters.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Flight purchases for both work and family travel.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Breakfast and parking are most important on early event mornings; dinner access becomes decisive after evening fairs, receptions, or late drives.
recovered_habits.default_action: Search practical chain or business hotels under the cap, verify breakfast hours and parking charges, and choose areas with nearby restaurants or reliable takeout.

evidence.quote: Hotels are the other piece. Breakfast included helps a lot on school-visit mornings, and I’d like not to be stranded for dinner after the Nampa fair. One queen bed is fine; I don’t need anything fancy.
For hotels, I need to stay inside the university reimbursement range, breakfast included if I can get it, and decent food nearby after the evening events. Nothing fancy.
Breakfast matters because first games can be early. Parking too. I don’t want a resort fee situation.
I would rather not pay downtown Portland parking. Breakfast at the hotels matters on Tuesday and Thursday because those mornings are early.
Breakfast and parking need to be in the approval note. The school visits start early enough that I do not want breakfast to be a mystery.
Breakfast and dinner access matter because the days are going to be weird. Flag that in the approval note.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Will give up included breakfast or accept paid parking when the official/closest hotel materially protects required sessions, winter walking, or a fixed morning event.
recovered_habits.name: Choose practical hotels with breakfast, clear parking, and nearby food over fancy properties
recovered_habits.preference_value: Prefers predictable, reimbursable hotels with breakfast, simple parking, and real dinner access; does not value luxury for these trips.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work recruitment/conference hotels and family sports-trip hotels, especially where mornings start early or evenings end late.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Cancellation window, local time cutoff, deposit/prepay terms, and exact room type must be clear before relying on a hold.
recovered_habits.default_action: Place refundable holds, track cancellation deadlines, keep backups only briefly, and release extras once the primary plan is safe.

evidence.quote: The block becomes basically nonrefundable after tomorrow night. I’m nervous because youth soccer schedules have lied to me before.
Breakfast by 6:30 would be ideal. I’d like cancellable at least to Feb 20. After Monday reception I may not eat until 8:45 or 9.
Yes: refundable, single queen room is fine, Delta if it’s comparable, and please request window seats. If a non-Delta nonstop is much better, I don’t need Delta for the sake of it.
The team block now only has nonrefundable rooms. A refundable hotel about 12 minutes farther has two queens, breakfast, and free parking. Help me choose.
Just me. Queen is fine, non-smoking, and no prepaid rates. I also want dinner access Sunday after landing.
Okay, I-15 side. No prepaid rooms. Queen if selectable, but flag it if the refundable inventory only shows something odd.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A stricter official block or less flexible rate is acceptable only when reimbursement/approval is clear and the convenience materially reduces trip risk.
recovered_habits.name: Prefer refundable, non-prepaid hotel holds while schedules are still moving
recovered_habits.preference_value: Strongly favors refundable/cancellable hotel rates and avoids prepaid or nonrefundable rooms while event times, brackets, or host details may change.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel planning before final agendas, tournament brackets, or host timing are fully stable.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: The extra night needs a clear reliability reason and should be avoided if same-day travel is genuinely safe.
recovered_habits.default_action: Use a previous-day arrival or earlier flight when a delay would make the first obligation stressful or risky.

evidence.quote: Sunday evening is less convenient at home, but I can justify it if the Monday risk is real.
Let’s not build the week around hoping the Monday flight runs perfectly. I can justify one extra hotel night if it keeps the reception day calm.
I’d rather not burn an extra night unless Sunday makes the reception risky.
I’d rather not be tense about a Monday arrival, but I also don’t want an unnecessary night if Monday morning is safe.
No prep before 1:00, but I cannot be late. The university will reimburse either airfare or mileage. An extra night should be okay if the reason is solid.
The Denver workshop agenda finally posted. Monday check-in is required by 12:30, so I agree the Monday morning flight is too risky.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Same-day arrival is acceptable when a clean early nonstop lands with ample cushion and the first agenda item is not mission-critical.
recovered_habits.name: Arrive the prior day or earlier when a same-day arrival would endanger a required event
recovered_habits.preference_value: Accepts an extra hotel night or earlier arrival when it protects a mandatory meeting, check-in, reception setup, or early breakfast.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Trips with fixed early-morning events, required badge pickup, setup deadlines, winter weather, or important first-day sessions.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: One controlled late-ish drive can be acceptable, but not repeated late drives, not rolling in after 11 if avoidable, and not when roads are bad.
recovered_habits.default_action: Place the overnight near the next fixed morning event or split the drive with a sensible intermediate stop.

evidence.quote: I’m okay with one longer post-fair drive, but not two in a row. I also don’t want to roll into a hotel after 11 if I can help it.
The reception could run to 8:45. I’d rather not do a long late drive after shaking hands all evening. Spokane Valley sounds okay if Tuesday morning isn’t awful.
That makes sense. I can handle one late-ish drive better than a pre-dawn one before a counselor breakfast.
I can leave Sunday after lunch, and I’d like to avoid heroic drives after a fair.
Finance would prefer one hotel night, but I can justify a second if driving home that late is a bad idea. I need the ranking.
I do not love hotel changes, but I hate the long late drive more.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Will accept a late drive if it clearly prevents a worse pre-dawn drive and conditions are dry/normal; will add an extra night if safety or fatigue makes the late return unreasonable.
recovered_habits.name: Avoid heroic late-night drives and pre-dawn gambles; move hotels when it protects the next event
recovered_habits.preference_value: Prefers to avoid long drives after evening events and very early drives before counselor breakfasts or school visits, even if that means another hotel move.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Road portions of work loops and family tournament trips, especially after fairs/receptions or before early check-ins.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Parking hassle, materials, number of cities, late-night movement, and risk of being stranded decide the choice more than the theoretical lowest cost.
recovered_habits.default_action: Rent a car for multi-stop recruitment loops; skip the rental and use airport rail/rideshare for downtown conferences or family trips with local rides.

evidence.quote: Do I really need a rental car? Parking in Seattle is never fun.
What about full rental car versus rideshares? I am not wild about driving I-35, but I also do not want to be stranded between events.
I really do not want a rental car downtown. Is the airport train reasonable on a Sunday afternoon?
Do I need a rental car because of the dinner move south?
I would also rather not rent a car unless it makes the weekend dramatically easier.
Yes, draft that note. Also ground transportation: no rental, right?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Even when a rental is kept for the route, use rideshare for a local urban dinner or event if parking is likely to be difficult.
recovered_habits.name: Use rental cars for dispersed/material-heavy routes, but avoid them for compact downtown conference trips
recovered_habits.preference_value: Prefers a rental car when events are spread across suburbs/cities or materials must move, but prefers rail/rideshare when the trip is a downtown, single-site conference with expensive parking.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Ground transport decisions after flight selection.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Luggage/materials should not be visible in the car; laptops, folio bags, badges, and high-value items travel inside with her.
recovered_habits.default_action: Decide what ships versus rides in the car, choose vehicle/cargo space accordingly, pre-plan garage/load-in, and separate each event’s materials before travel.

evidence.quote: I’m mostly worried about the luggage sitting in the car during lunch.
I also don't want luggage visible in the car during the Vancouver transfer table.
Probably five boxes plus the banner tube if I don't ship.
Two medium boxes, tablecloth, retractable banner, laptop bag. I can ship one box to Boise if that makes flying workable.
Can you map the materials handoff points? That’s the part my supervisor keeps asking about.
Materials can ship to Plano but not Austin.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If shipping is unavailable or material volume is too high, driving or an SUV rental becomes the fallback even if flying would otherwise be attractive.
recovered_habits.name: Plan materials logistics explicitly before booking the route
recovered_habits.preference_value: Treats recruitment boxes, banner tubes, laptops, and luggage as routing constraints that require shipping, cargo, parking, and security plans rather than improvisation.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Admissions/recruitment trips with brochure boxes, banners, display materials, or luggage left between stops.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Documentation is most important when finance or a director may question a higher fare, one-way drop fee, official block, or non-obvious routing choice.
recovered_habits.default_action: Save itemized receipts/folios, parking/toll/fuel records when applicable, cancellation screenshots, fare comparisons, and a concise rationale for the selected plan.

evidence.quote: Perfect. Can you give me the final booking summary in travel-request language?
Anything else to note for reimbursement?
Receipts and checkout stuff?
Our office will pay a reasonable nonstop if the schedule makes sense. I just need clean documentation.
Receipt list? My director will ask about the one-way car.
Last piece: mileage, parking, and meal receipts. The garage receipt is the one I’m most likely to forget.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: For mileage trips, fuel may be covered by mileage rather than reimbursed separately, but she still wants route/mileage and key parking/meal receipts organized.
recovered_habits.name: Keep clean reimbursement documentation and decision rationales
recovered_habits.preference_value: Wants final travel-request language, reimbursement notes, receipt lists, and comparison rationale for choices that cost more but reduce risk.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work travel bookings, especially open-jaw flights, one-way rentals, above-cap hotels, parking-heavy venues, and mileage trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: The room type must be explicit rather than run-of-house or requested-only when bed setup matters.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book a specific, non-smoking queen/king for solo travel and a guaranteed two-queen room for family trips with teens or gear.

evidence.quote: One queen bed is fine; I don’t need anything fancy.
Room types: I’m solo, so one queen or king is fine. I don’t want a double-double unless that’s all that’s left.
It’s me, Miguel, and Sofia. Sofia needs her own bed. Two queens sounds easier than a sleeper sofa after a late drive.
We need a real two-queen room, not a sofa-bed setup, and breakfast at the hotel would help.
We need one room with two queens, parking, and breakfast if possible. I do not want to be hunting for food before a 7 a.m. warmup.
Just me. Queen is fine, non-smoking, and no prepaid rates. I also want dinner access Sunday after landing.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A king is acceptable for solo travel if refundable and non-smoking; double/double or sofa-bed setups are fallback only when no better refundable option exists.
recovered_habits.name: Match room type to traveler group: simple single bed solo, real two queens for family or teen trips
recovered_habits.preference_value: For solo work travel, a non-smoking queen or king is fine; for family/tournament travel, wants a real two-queen room and avoids sofa-bed or vague bedding setups.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel room selection for both solo work trips and family sports/family trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Cold/dry roads are acceptable; active snow/ice, closures, traction controls, severe gusts, or forecasted travel-time blowups trigger a change.
recovered_habits.default_action: Check road/weather status before travel, leave earlier or add a buffer only when road conditions justify it, and keep the base plan if conditions are merely cold but dry.

evidence.quote: Snow is now in the I-80 forecast, so driving feels like a bad idea.
We cannot leave SLC before 4:15 Friday, and the forecast has blowing snow around Twin Falls.
I can do the late drive if it is cold and dry. I do not want to do it in active snow or ice. University vehicle is approved now, so use that assumption.
Also the forecast shows gusts on I-15. Can you tighten the timing instead of changing reservations?
Delta shifted the Sunday outbound by 18 minutes later, and now there is a Front Range storm forecast Sunday night. I do not want to rebuild the trip, just tell me if I should move earlier.

Forecast now shows a snow band on I-84 between Burley and Twin Falls Tuesday morning, and the Boise venue moved the materials drop to 3:30 PM. Nampa says they can do a grab-and-go breakfast. Also, the restaurant closest to the Pocatello hotel is closed Wednesday. I’d like to avoid rebuilding the trip unless Tuesday gets too tight.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If a storm threatens the flight/road window but does not yet overlap the actual travel time, keep the plan and monitor for waivers or updated road alerts.
recovered_habits.name: Use weather-triggered pivots for winter driving rather than rebuilding prematurely
recovered_habits.preference_value: Avoids active snow, ice, closures, heavy gusts, or road-warning drives, but does not want to rebuild a trip unless the forecast crosses a real risk threshold.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Winter or shoulder-season road trips and flight timing decisions involving I-80, I-84, I-15, Denver/Front Range, Idaho, and tournament travel.
